title: Click Guard → Automatic and manual blocks

steps.caption: Blocked IPs
steps.narration: Click Guard blocks repeat offenders on its own, and you can block any address yourself. Here's both.

steps.caption: The Source column
steps.narration: The Source column says which: auto, or manual.

steps.caption: Blocked on its own
steps.narration: This address was flagged and made eleven visits in an hour, so Click Guard blocked it. The source reads auto.

steps.caption: A range, blocked by hand
steps.narration: A manual block can be a whole range, written as CIDR.

steps.caption: Type a wildcard
steps.narration: To block one yourself, type it here. A wildcard like this covers every address that starts the same way.

steps.caption: On the list, marked manual
steps.narration: It joins the list, marked manual.

steps.caption: An IPv6 address
steps.narration: IPv6 addresses work the same way.

steps.caption: Collapse the section menu
steps.narration: Collapse the section menu to give the tables more room.

steps.caption: Clicks report
steps.narration: In the Clicks report, each visit has a Block button of its own, at the end of the row.

steps.caption: Block this visitor
steps.narration: Choose it and that visitor's IP goes on the list too.

steps.caption: Unblock
steps.narration: Changed your mind? The X on a blocked row unblocks it.

steps.caption: Off the list
steps.narration: The wildcard is off the list. Blocked addresses stay until you remove them.

steps.caption: Menu: Click Guard
steps.narration: Blocked IPs lives under Traffic signals, in Click Guard, first in the rail on the left.

youtube.title: How to block and unblock IPs in Click Guard | ConstructHUB
youtube.description: How blocking works in Click Guard in ConstructHUB. Flagged repeat visitors are blocked automatically and marked auto; you can block a single IPv4 or IPv6 address, a CIDR range or a wildcard yourself, block a visitor straight from the Clicks report, and unblock any row with one click.
